{{Top}}
[[File:HoloNet-FF88.png|thumb|right|250px|The logo of the HoloNet]]
{{Quote|Tell these superiors of yours that if my demands are not met within the next ten minutes, I will personally disembowel Supreme Chancellor Palpatine live on the HoloNet. Am I understood?|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], to [[Lieutenant Commander/Legends|Lieutenant Commander]] [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
The '''HoloNet''', also spelled '''Holonet''', was a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] communications grid that was developed, used and maintained by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and later by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The HoloNet was a near-instantaneous communications network commissioned by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] to provide a free flow of [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] communication and information exchange among member [[Planet/Legends|worlds]]. It vastly sped up galactic communications, which had previously depended on more circuitous [[Subspace/Legends|subspace]] transmissions or relays.

==System==
[[File:HoloNetSpeech-POP.png|thumb|left|230px|[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] address to the senate is broadcast over the HoloNet]]
A message was first broadcast from a planet, a vessel in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], or from another point of origin; from there, it was then routed from the point of origin's transmitter through potentially millions of [[Hyperwave transceiver/Legends|hyperwave transceivers]] suspended in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] to a [[HoloNet relay/Legends|HoloNet relay]], where it was sorted, identified and logged by the relay's computer, and then routed further via appropriate transceivers to its destination. The transceivers themselves transferred information across the galaxy through [[Simu-tunnel/Legends|s-threads]]. This enabled data to be sent and received at faster-than-[[Lightspeed/Legends|light speeds]], ensuring near-instantaneous communication from one end of the galaxy to the other, by routing information from origin, to transceiver, to HoloNet relay, to transceiver network yet again, and finally to its destination.

It should also be noted that information transmitted via the HoloNet was nearly impossible to infiltrate or corrupt, thanks to the s-thread's incredibly narrow hyperspace dimensions. The only way to do so was to attach a listening device to the sender's equipment, the relay station, or at the destination itself.

The HoloNet system was an extremely costly expenditure, both for transceiver placement/maintenance (funded by the government) and for consumer HoloNet equipment. However, it was one of the major methods of communication in the galaxy.
One of HoloNet's services was the "[[Imperial.emp]]," a service that even [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] used.
HoloNet was also known for containing numerous forums, including one called the [[Naboo message exchange]].

==History==
A predecessor to the HoloNet called the [[holonet entertainment system]] was in use among [[Tythan|the people]] of the [[Settled Worlds]] in the centuries prior to the Republic's founding, providing entertainment aboard the pre-[[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] [[Tython system/Legends|Tythan]] ships such as the [[Peacemaker-class cruiser|''Peacemaker''-class]].<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void">''[[Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void]]''</ref> Prior to the HoloNet's founding, the ancient galaxy relied on ships uploading and downloading data packets as they travelled up and down star lanes.<ref name=":0" />

Created thanks to the Galactic Senate's efforts several thousand years [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the HoloNet quickly expanded throughout the galaxy, ending up with at least one emitter/receiver device located on virtually every planet of the Galactic Republic. The Holonet was operational by at least [[3954 BBY]].<ref name="The Old Republic: Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> The massive computer sorter and decoder infrastructure needed to maintain a galactic communication network was incredibly complicated and expensive to maintain, but various governments and corporations subsidized it since it was the HoloNet that held the Old Republic together.<ref name=":0">[[Galaxywide NewsNets|''Galaxywide NewsNets'']]</ref>

[[File:Holonet.jpg|thumb|250px|A HoloNet transmission from a [[Gran/Legends|Gran]]]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], plans to expand the HoloNet to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] were delayed due to budgetary restructuring according to the [[General Ministry Communications Agency]]. 250,000 worlds in several sectors, including [[Portmoak sector/Legends|Portmoak]], [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis]], [[Parmic sector/Legends|Parmic]], [[Quence sector/Legends|Quence]], and [[Kathol sector/Legends|Kathol]], were not to see access for one fiscal year. Where they lacked in primary HoloNet conduits, they made up for with a network of [[Subspace relay station/Legends|Subspace relay stations]] for intersector communications, resulting in delayed galactic news reaching those sectors within days or weeks.<ref name="HoloNet News Vol. 531 48">[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 48|''HoloNet News Vol. 531'' #48]] - Outer Rim HoloNet Expansion Delayed''</ref>

During the Clone Wars, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy]] created the [[Shadowfeed/Legends|CIS Shadowfeed]], a network of [[Hyperwave transceiver/Legends|hyperwave transceivers]] similar to the Republic's [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] channel. During this time, both sides used the HoloNet to broadcast propaganda. Large portions of the HoloNet were also damaged or fell out of use. The vast network of transceivers had fallen into disrepair as corrupt senators diverted allocated repair funds for their own purposes.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook" />

When [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] assumed power, large portions of the HoloNet were shut down to prevent news of the Empire's atrocities from spreading quickly. While the network remained active in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] and was used for military communications among the Imperial fleet, systems beyond the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] were cut off to isolate them and limit the spread of information. In the early days of the Empire, many transceivers that had been in civilian hands were seized and installed in the growing fleet of Star Destroyers. During the time of the Empire, the HoloNet was strictly controlled, used mostly for [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] communications. This greatly inhibited the ability of groups like the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] to communicate, and arguably also had an isolating effect on the many planets over which the Empire held power. By the time of the Battle of Yavin, only media outlets that have been properly licensed and censored by imperial bureaucrats, the military, and agencies managed by planetary Governors and Grand Moffs could legally use the HoloNet.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook>''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> 

The Empire's drastic censorship didn't shut down the flow of information for long. Trading firms, financial exchanges, and various governments restored HoloNet access by outfitting the fastest ships commercially available with sophisticated broadcasting gear. These information courier shuttles were sent up and down the trade corridors, system by system, reverting from hyperspace only long enough to uplink and downlink huge message packets before moving on. Once fully automated courier droids replaced these shuttles, major HoloNet networks were able to resume broadcasting, though with a perceptible timelag between transmission and reception. This system replicated an ancient method of galactic communication before the creation of the HoloNet. It was a loose conglomeration of sanctioned and pirate networks that collectively became known as the [[NewsNet|NewsNets]]. During this period, [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab]] created an [[Baobab HoloNet|alternative HoloNet]] since the official HoloNet disseminated only Imperial propaganda without the "complication" of unapproved free speech. After the Empire fell, HoloNet channels were reopened and security was lifted, restoring free speech.<ref name=":0" />

Near the end of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] succeeded in disabling the entire network. It resumed functioning shortly after the invasion had been thwarted.

After the Yuuzhan Vong War, many smaller vessels, such as [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]], were equipped with HoloNet receivers and transmitters, including [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo's]] own modified [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class shuttle]].

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:HoloNet_icon.jpg|thumb|70px|In-game HoloNet icon in ''Star Wars: Tiny Death Star'']]
In the non-[[canon]] mobile game ''[[Star Wars: Tiny Death Star]]'', the HoloNet feed was portrayed similar to a real-world social media platform such as [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] or [[Wikipedia:Facebook|Facebook]], where NPCs known as [[bitizen]]s could post statuses and other bitizens could "like" them.<ref name="tiny">''[[Star Wars: Tiny Death Star]]''</ref>
